Keir Starmer breaks his silence as questions swirl around Peter Mandelson’s links to the Epstein files — and the language is careful, coded, managerial. When he talks about Labour needing to avoid “a fight with itself,” that’s read as a euphemism for internal corruption and elite compromise, not party unity. The reaction cuts between Starmer’s attempt at steady leadership and the argument that establishment politics itself is exhausted — filtered, evasive, out of step with a public that’s done with managed narratives. Reform is framed as the coming threat, but the deeper claim is that the real crisis isn’t factional — it’s systemic.
